Note::contains¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

std::vector<std::uint8_t> Note::contains(std::string_view needle) const

Test Every Cell For A Literal Substring¶

contains(needle) reports, for each text cell, whether needle occurs anywhere inside it. It is the predicate half of the substring family: use it to build a mask for filtering, counting, or branching, when the question is “which cells mention this?” rather than “rewrite the matches” (that is replace / remove_all) or “pull the matches out” (that is regex_findall).

The match is a literal byte-substring search — no regular-expression metacharacters, no word boundaries, no normalization. needle and the cell are compared exactly as stored, so the test is case-sensitive and byte-oriented; fold case first with lower when you want a case-insensitive check.

Return value¶

The result is not a Note. It is a flat std::vector<std::uint8_t> with one entry per cell — 1 where needle was found, 0 where it was not — in row-major order. For a rank-0 Note the vector has one entry; for a rank-2 or rank-3 Note the cells are flattened in the same order print walks them. The length always equals numel().

Returning a plain std::uint8_t vector (rather than a boolean Series) keeps the predicate cheap and lets you feed it straight into indexing loops or into pluss::make_series if you want Series-side masking.

Edge cases¶

  • An empty needle is contained in every cell, including empty cells, so every entry is 1.

  • A needle longer than a cell can never match that cell: its entry is 0.

  • The scan is linear in total input size and does no allocation beyond the result vector.

Example 1: A Basic Mask¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note({"midterm_1", "final_exam", "quiz"});
const auto mask = n.contains("exam");
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < mask.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << static_cast<int>(mask[i]);
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[0, 1, 0]

Only "final_exam" contains the substring exam.

Example 2: The Test Is Case-Sensitive¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note({"midterm_1", "final_exam", "quiz"});
const auto mask = n.contains("EXAM");
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < mask.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << static_cast<int>(mask[i]);
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[0, 0, 0]

"EXAM" is a different byte sequence from "exam".

Example 3: Fold Case First For A Case-Insensitive Check¶

const auto mask =
    pluss::make_note({"Exam 1", "FINAL EXAM", "Quiz"}).lower().contains("exam");
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < mask.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << static_cast<int>(mask[i]);
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[1, 1, 0]

Example 4: An Empty Needle Matches Everything¶

const auto mask = pluss::make_note({"abc", "", "x"}).contains("");
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < mask.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << static_cast<int>(mask[i]);
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[1, 1, 1]

Example 5: A Needle Longer Than The Cell Never Matches¶

const auto mask = pluss::make_note({"ab"}).contains("abcd");
std::cout << "[" << static_cast<int>(mask[0]) << "]\n";

Output¶

[0]

Example 6: Higher-Rank Input Is Flattened Row-Major¶

const auto mask =
    pluss::make_note({{"apple", "grape"}, {"plum", "pear"}}).contains("p");
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < mask.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << static_cast<int>(mask[i]);
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[1, 1, 1, 1]

Four cells, flattened in row-major order; every one contains a p.

See Also¶

  • Note::regex_findall: when you need the matching substrings, not just a yes/no.

  • Note::replace / Note::remove_all: rewrite or delete matches instead of testing for them.

  • Note::lower: normalize case before a case-insensitive test.
